questions.q: In a solution the quantity of common salt in 320 gm water is 31 gm. Calculate the concentration \% of the solution in context of mass by mass percentage.
questions.s:
Dekh bhai, sabse pehle Core Conceptual Tool: 5. Unitary Scaling trigger hoga yahan. Pen-Free Observation: Dekh bhai, total mass $320+31 = 351$ gram hai. Ab 351 ka $10\%$ lagbhag $35.1$ hota hai. Apna solute sirf 31 gram hai, jo $35.1$ se thoda kam hai. Iska seedha matlab hai answer $10\%$ se thoda sa niche hoga. Options dekh, sirf ek hi value match kar rahi hai $8.83\%$. Method 1 (Ninja Technique / Exam Approach): Bina pen uthaye approximation maar. $\\frac{31}{351} \\approx \\frac{31}{350}$. Aur $350$ ka $9\%$ hota hai $31.5$. Toh answer $9\%$ se bhi margin sa chhota hoga. Seedha Option 1 uda de! Method 2 (Concept Builder): Formula lagana hai toh: $\\frac{\\text{Mass of Solute}}{\\text{Mass of Solution}} \\times 100$. Yahan Solution = Solute + Solvent = $31 + 320 = 351$ gm. Concentration = $\\frac{31}{351} \\times 100 = 8.831\\%$. Exam Takeaway: CGL me exact division karke decimal me time waste nahi karna hai, denominator dekhte hi approximation lagana seekh aur option eliminate kar!
ConceptFormula / Hack
Mass %$(\\frac{\\text{Solute}}{\\text{Total Solution}}) \\times 100$

questions.q: Population of a city X is 4,25,000. In the next three years, there is a total increase of $12\%$ in male population and increase of $20\%$ in female population, which results in male to female ratio as x:y. If the original male and female population of the city is 2,50,000 and 1,75,000 respectively, then find the value of (4x+5y).
questions.s:
Dekh bhai, yahan par Core Conceptual Tool: 2. Successive Change (The Chain Reaction) ke multipliers kaam aayenge. Pen-Free Observation: Bhai zeros se dosti tod de. Original Male 250 aur Female 175 maan le. Zeros end me waise bhi ratio me kat jayenge. Male badh raha hai $12\%$ se (multiplier 1.12) aur female $20\%$ se (multiplier 1.2). Method 1 (Ninja Technique / Exam Approach): Seedha ratio likh! Naye Male $= 250 \\times 1.12 = 280$. Nayi Female $= 175 \\times 1.2 = 210$. Ratio $x:y = 280:210 = 4:3$. Ab $x=4$ aur $y=3$ mil gaya, seedha eq me put kar: $4(4) + 5(3) = 16 + 15 = 31$. Khatam! Method 2 (Concept Builder): Agar proper solve karna hai toh: Naya Male $= 2,50,000 + (12\\% \\text{ of } 2,50,000) = 2,80,000$. Nayi Female $= 1,75,000 + (20\\% \\text{ of } 1,75,000) = 2,10,000$. Ratio $x/y = 28/21 = 4/3$. Phir equation solve kar lo. Par time zyada lagega. Exam Takeaway: Zeros ko dimaag me hi kaat dena chahiye ratio nikalte waqt, ye best time saver hai.
Multiplier TipAction
Increase by R%Multiply by $(1 + \\frac{R}{100})$

questions.q: An ore contains $25\%$ of an alloy that has $90\%$ iron. Other than this, in the remaining $75\%$ of the ore, there is no iron. How many kilograms of the ore are needed to obtain 60 kg of pure iron?
questions.s:
Dekh bhai, yahan par Core Conceptual Tool: 1. CPR (Constant Product Ratio) / Successive Fraction trigger hoga. Pen-Free Observation: Dekh, poore ore me loha (iron) kahan se aa raha hai? Sirf uss $25\%$ wale hisse se. Aur usme bhi pura loha nahi hai, uska bhi $90\%$ hai. Toh overall iron kitna hua? $25\\% \\times 90\\%$. Method 1 (Ninja Technique / Exam Approach): Overall iron nikal: $25\\%$ yani $\\frac{1}{4}$. Iska $90\\%$ hoga $22.5\\%$. Matlab agar total ore $X$ hai, toh $X \\times 22.5\\% = 60$ kg. Seedha divide maar: $X = \\frac{60}{0.225} = \\frac{60000}{225}$. $25$ se kaat: $\\frac{2400}{9} = \\frac{800}{3} = 266.67$ kg. Ud gaya sawal! Method 2 (Concept Builder): Maan lo Total Ore = $100x$. Usme Alloy hai $25x$. Ab is $25x$ me Iron hai $90\\%$ of $25x = 22.5x$. Given hai $22.5x = 60 \\implies x = \\frac{60}{22.5}$. Hamein chahiye $100x$, toh $100 \\times \\frac{60}{22.5} = 266.67$ kg. Exam Takeaway: Percentage of percentage ko hamesha multiply karke net percentage banaya kar, bahut time bachega.
StepCalculation
Net Iron %$25\\% \\times 90\\% = 22.5\\%$

questions.q: The price of petrol shot up by $5\%$. Before the hike, the price was $\text{Rs. } 82$ per litre. A man travels 3045 km every month and his car gives mileage of 15 km per litre. What is the increase the monthly expenditure (to the nearest Rs.) on the man's travel due to the hike in the petrol in prices?
questions.s:
Dekh bhai, yahan par Core Conceptual Tool: 5. Unitary Scaling ka basic fundaa lagega. Pen-Free Observation: Gadhe bachhe pura purana kharcha nikalenge aur naya kharcha nikal ke minus karenge. Apne ko smart banna hai! Sirf "increase" pucha hai, toh sirf "increased price" pe focus karenge. Method 1 (Ninja Technique / Exam Approach): Petrol ki extra keemat kitni badhi? $82$ ka $5\\%$. $10\\%$ hota hai $8.2$, toh $5\\%$ hua $\\text{Rs. } 4.1$ per litre. Ab total petrol kitna lagta hai mahine me? $3045 \\text{ km} / 15 \\text{ km/L} = 203$ litres. Toh extra kharcha = $203 \\times 4.1 = 832.3$. Approximation se seedha 832 tick kar! Method 2 (Concept Builder): Old Exp = $203 \\text{ L} \\times 82 = 16646$. New Price = $82 + 4.1 = 86.1$. New Exp = $203 \\times 86.1 = 17478.3$. Difference = $17478.3 - 16646 = 832.3$. Itna lamba karke exam me kya gold medal milega? Exam Takeaway: Humesha direct difference (delta) pe kaam kar, absolute values calculate karne me time kharab mat kar.
Smart TrickLogic
Delta ExpenditureQuantity Consumed $\\times$ Rate Increase

questions.q: Which of the following is the <u>least</u>? (CHSL TIER I-$\frac{13}{11}$/2025-SHIFT 3)
questions.s:
Dekh bhai, yahan par Core Conceptual Tool: 5. Unitary Scaling / Basic Calculation ka quick mental maths check hai. Pen-Free Observation: Zeros ko udana seekh. Percentage ka $\\frac{1}{100}$ do zeros ko kaat deta hai. Toh bas numbers ko multiply karna hai. Method 1 (Ninja Technique / Exam Approach): A. $2 \\times 38 = 76$ B. $25 \\times 3 = 75$ C. $18 \\times 4.5 = 81$ (Ya aise dekh $18\\% \\times 450 = 9\\% \\times 900 = 81$) D. $3 \\times 24 = 72$ Saaf dikh raha hai 72 sabse chhota hai. Seedha option D tick kar. Method 2 (Concept Builder): Likh ke kaatne wale bache $\\frac{20}{100} \\times 380$ karenge aur time barbaad karenge. CGL aur CHSL me in lallu sawalo pe pen nahi uthaya jata! Exam Takeaway: Humesha $A\\% \\text{ of } B = B\\% \\text{ of } A$ aur zero-cancelling technique ka use kar.
ValueCalculation
30% of 240$3 \\times 24 = 72$ (Minimum)

questions.q: In an examination, (A + 6)% of the students failed in Mathematics and (A - 8)% failed in Science. $28\%$ of the students failed in both the subjects. If the percentage of students who passed in both the subjects was $50\%$, then what is the value of A?
questions.s:
Dekh bhai, yahan par Core Conceptual Tool: Set Theory / Venn Diagram lagega. Pen-Free Observation: Total bachhe 100% hote hain. Jo dono me pass hue wo $50\%$ hain, toh jo kisi na kisi me fail hue (kam se kam ek me) wo bache hue $100 - 50 = 50\%$ honge. Method 1 (Ninja Technique / Exam Approach): Universal rule laga $n(M \\cup S) = n(M) + n(S) - n(M \\cap S)$. Fail hone walon ka union = $50\\%$. Equation rakh: $50 = (A + 6) + (A - 8) - 28$. Solve kar: $50 = 2A - 30 \\implies 2A = 80 \\implies A = 40$. Mental math ka asli khel hai, pen ki zarurat bas equation likhne me thi! Method 2 (Concept Builder): Venn diagram bana le dimaag me. Only Math fail $= A + 6 - 28 = A - 22$. Only Science fail $= A - 8 - 28 = A - 36$. Both fail $= 28$. Total Fail $= (A - 22) + (A - 36) + 28 = 2A - 30$. Ye barabar hoga $100\\% - \\text{Passed in Both}(50\\%) = 50\\%$. Toh $2A - 30 = 50 \\implies A = 40$. Exam Takeaway: Venn diagram draw karne me time kharab mat kar, seedha $A \\cup B$ wala equation dimag me set rakh.
Venn ConceptFormula
Total Union$n(A \\cup B) = n(A) + n(B) - n(A \\cap B)$

questions.q: A stock portfolio consists of four stocks. Stock A represents $10\%$ of the portfolio and has a return of $4\%$. Stock B represents $20\%$ of the portfolio and has a return of $8\%$. Stock C represents $30\%$ of the portfolio and has a return of $3\%$. Stock D represents the remaining $40\%$ of the portfolio and has a <u>negative-return</u> of $6\%$. What is the average return of the portfolio?
questions.s:
Dekh bhai, yahan par Core Conceptual Tool: 3. JSM (Junior Satisfaction Method) / Deviation or Weighted Average lagega. Pen-Free Observation: Yahan seedha portfolio ke weights ko returns se multiply karna hai. Positive returns add honge aur negative wala subtract hoga. Base hamesha total weight $100\\%$ rahega. Method 1 (Ninja Technique / Exam Approach): Values ko direct multiply karke add maar de: A: $10 \\times 4 = +40$ B: $20 \\times 8 = +160$ C: $30 \\times 3 = +90$ D: $40 \\times (-6) = -240$ Total $= 40 + 160 + 90 - 240 = 290 - 240 = 50$. Average return $= \\frac{50}{100} = 0.5\\%$. Khatam baat, koi extra step nahi! Method 2 (Concept Builder): Formula hota hai $\\frac{w_1r_1 + w_2r_2 + w_3r_3 + w_4r_4}{w_1+w_2+w_3+w_4}$. Par exam me formula likhne thodi baithega? Seedha net effect nikal aur total weight se divide kar. Exam Takeaway: Weighted average ke questions me negative values pe dhyan dena, silly mistake se bacha layega.
MethodCalculation Flow
Weighted Sum$\\Sigma (Weight \\times Return) / \\Sigma Weight$

questions.q: If $65\%$ of 350 - ?% of 250 + $40\%$ of 120 = 158, then find the value of ?
questions.s:
Dekh bhai, yahan Core Conceptual Tool: 5. Unitary Scaling aur thoda Digital Sum (C9) ka magic chalega. Pen-Free Observation: Equation ko seedha simplify kar. $40\\%$ of 120 toh lallu hai, seedha 48. $65\\%$ of 350 thoda calculative hai par isko decimal $0.65 \\times 350$ likh sakte hain. Method 1 (Ninja Technique / Exam Approach): Solve kar dimaag me: $65\\% \\text{ of } 350 = 350 \\times \\frac{65}{100} = 3.5 \\times 65 = 227.5$. $40\\% \\text{ of } 120 = 48$. Equation banegi: $227.5 - 2.5x + 48 = 158$. $275.5 - 2.5x = 158 \\implies 2.5x = 117.5$. Decimal hata de, $25x = 1175 \\implies x = 47$. Method 2 (Concept Builder - Digital Sum / C9): Digital sum nikal equation ka: $65\\%$ (DS = 2) of 350 (DS = 8) $\\rightarrow 2 \\times 8 = 16 \\rightarrow$ DS = 7. $40\\%$ (DS = 4) of 120 (DS = 3) $\\rightarrow 4 \\times 3 = 12 \\rightarrow$ DS = 3. $158$ ka DS $= 1+5+8 = 14 \\rightarrow 5$. $x \\% \\text{ of } 250$ (DS = 7) $= 7x$. Equation DS: $7 - 7x + 3 = 5 \\implies 10 - 7x = 5 \\implies 7x = 5$. Kaunsa option 7 se multiply hoke DS 5 dega? Option A (47 -> DS 2) $\\implies 7 \\times 2 = 14 \\implies DS 5$. Boom! Exam Takeaway: Digital sum wahan lagao jahan normal calculation time le rahi ho.
Smart HackUsage
Digital Sum (C9)Match DS of LHS and RHS options

questions.q: If the first number is $15\%$ less than the third number and the ratio of the second and third numbers is 3: 5, then by what percentage is the average of the first and third numbers more than the second number?
questions.s:
Dekh bhai, is sawal me Core Conceptual Tool: 4. Cross-Product Method / Ratio Shifting ki jarurat hai. Pen-Free Observation: Sabse best tareeqa hai Third number ko 100 maan lena. Isse calculations ekdum butter ho jayengi. Method 1 (Ninja Technique / Exam Approach): Let Third = 100. First usse $15\\%$ kam hai $\\implies$ First = 85. Second aur Third ka ratio 3:5 hai. Agar 5 unit = 100, toh 1 unit = 20, matlab Second = 60 hua. Ab First aur Third ka Average nikal = $\\frac{85 + 100}{2} = 92.5$. Ye average Second(60) se kitna zyada hai? Gap = $92.5 - 60 = 32.5$. Percentage More = $\\frac{32.5}{60} \\times 100 = \\frac{325}{6} = 54.16\\%$. Direct jumps maar approach me! Method 2 (Concept Builder): Agar variables me phansega toh: $z = x$, $y = 0.85x$, $y/z = 3/5$... ye sab karne me poora minute chala jayega. Humesha Base 100 pakdo aisi situations me. Exam Takeaway: Jab bhi percentages aur ratios mixed aayein, common element ko 100 ka multiple maano.
Base Shift RuleApplication
Set Common BaseMake Third Number = 100

questions.q: A solution of sugar and milk contains $26\%$ sugar by weight. After boiling, 63 kg milk evaporates and the solution now contains $40\%$ of sugar. Find the original quantity of solution?
questions.s:
Dekh bhai, yahan par lagta hai apna deadly Core Conceptual Tool: 1. CPR (Constant Product Ratio). Pen-Free Observation: Boil karne par pani ya doodh udata hai, cheeni (sugar) toh wahi rehti hai. Solid part humesha constant rahega. Bas yahi equation banani hai. Method 1 (Ninja Technique / Exam Approach): Equate solid parts: $26\\%$ of Old Solution = $40\\%$ of New Solution. Ratio of Old to New Solution = $40 : 26 = 20 : 13$. Yani pehle 20 unit the, ab 13 unit bache. Kitne unit udd gaye? 7 units. Question me diya hai 63 kg evaporate hua. Toh 7 units = 63 kg $\\implies$ 1 unit = 9 kg. Original quantity puchi hai, yani 20 units. $20 \\times 9 = 180$ kg. Answer aa gaya 10 second me! Method 2 (Concept Builder): Let initial quantity be $x$. Sugar = $0.26x$. Final quantity = $x - 63$. Sugar = $0.40(x - 63)$. Since sugar is constant: $0.26x = 0.40x - 25.2 \\implies 0.14x = 25.2 \\implies x = 180$. Par ye CGL ka approach nahi hai. Exam Takeaway: Mixture me jo cheez evaporate/add nahi hoti, hamesha usi ko equate kiya kar!
Trick (Solid Constancy)Logic
% Change vs Qty Change$P_1 \\times Q_1 = P_2 \\times Q_2$

questions.q: In Veeru Bhai Pvt. limited company $60\%$ of the employees are men and $48\%$ of the employees are engineers and $66.66\%$ of these are men. The percentage of women who are <u>not</u> engineers:
questions.s:
Dekh bhai, ye Core Conceptual Tool: 5. Unitary Scaling / Tree Diagram ka classic question hai. Pen-Free Observation: Jab percentage of percentages khela ja raha ho, total employees ko 100 maan lo. Language ki trap pakadni hai, poocha kiske reference me hai ye dekhna zaroori hai. Method 1 (Ninja Technique / Exam Approach): Total = 100. Men = 60, toh Women = 40. Engineers = 48. Inme se $66.66\\%$ (yani $\\frac{2}{3}$) Men hain. Male Engineers = $\\frac{2}{3} \\times 48 = 32$. Toh Female Engineers bachi = $48 - 32 = 16$. Ab Non-Engineer Women nikalni hai: Total Women(40) - Female Engineers(16) = 24. Question ne pucha hai "percentage of women who are not engineers" (yani base "women" ka hai). Toh $\\frac{24}{40} \\times 100 = 60\\%$. Method 2 (Concept Builder): Agar language dhyan se nahi padhega, toh tu $24\\%$ (out of total) likh aayega aur options me dhundhega. Examiner ki chaal yahi hoti hai "percentage of women" matlab base 40 rahega, 100 nahi. Exam Takeaway: Percentage kiske "respect" me pucha hai (Base), usko hamesha underline kar!
Language TrapCorrect Base
"% of women who are..."Denominator is Total Women, not Total Employees

questions.q: A milkman bought 50 litres of milk for $\text{Rs. } 2000$. 5 litres spoiled. At what rate per litre should he sell the remaining milk to make a profit of $20\%$ on his total outlay?
questions.s:
Dekh bhai, ye seedha Core Conceptual Tool: 5. Unitary Scaling / Target Value ka sawaal hai. Pen-Free Observation: Milkman ko sirf apne total kharche pe 20% profit nikalna hai. Use ghanta farq padta hai kitna doodh fuk gaya, bas vasooli bache doodh se karni hai. Method 1 (Ninja Technique / Exam Approach): Total investment = $\\text{Rs. } 2000$. Target vasooli (20% profit ke sath) = $2000 \\times 1.2 = \\text{Rs. } 2400$. Doodh bacha kitna? $50 - 5 = 45$ litres. Bas, $2400$ nikalne hain 45 litre bech ke. Rate $= \\frac{2400}{45} = \\frac{480}{9} = \\frac{160}{3} = 53.33$. Faltu ka cost price per litre nikal ke time pass nahi karna! Method 2 (Concept Builder): CP of 1L = 40. Pura milk bigad gaya, waisa logic lagane lagega toh ulajh jayega. Profit is always on total Capital Expended, not per unit unless quantity is fully sold. Exam Takeaway: Target total revenue nikal aur divided by remaining quantity kar de. Best hack!
Pricing HackFormula
New SP per UnitTarget Total Revenue / Remaining Quantity

questions.q: In a speed test a student got $30\%$ marks and failed by 25 marks. In the same speed test another student got $40\%$ marks and secured $25\%$ marks more than the essential minimum marks. Then max. marks set for speed test?
questions.s:
Dekh bhai, ye hai Core Conceptual Tool: 3. Deviation / Gap Equating ka masaledar version. Pen-Free Observation: Do situations di hain, dono ko Passing Marks (PM) ke reference me equate karna hai. Method 1 (Ninja Technique / Exam Approach): Pehle bacche ke Passing Marks = $30\\% \\text{ of M} + 25$. Dusra baccha laya hai $40\\%$ marks, jo Passing Marks se $25\\%$ zyada hain. Matlab $1.25 \\times \\text{Passing Marks} = 40\\% \\text{ of M}$. $\\implies \\text{Passing Marks} = \\frac{40\\%}{1.25} = 32\\% \\text{ of M}$. Ab dekh, dono passing marks ko equate kar! $30\\% + 25 = 32\\% \\implies 2\\% = 25$ marks. Agar $2\\%$ marks 25 hain, toh $100\\%$ marks (Total) $= 25 \\times 50 = 1250$. Bina badi equations likhe solve! Method 2 (Concept Builder): $0.4M = 1.25(0.3M + 25)$. Isko khologe toh aayega $0.4M = 0.375M + 31.25 \\implies 0.025M = 31.25 \\implies M = 1250$. Ye bhi theek hai par Ninja technique me calculations aasaan ho gayi. Exam Takeaway: Pass/Fail marks ko ek single reference variable pe le aao (yaha passing marks ko pakda) aur equation equate kardo.
Equating MethodLogic
Find common anchor$PM_1 = PM_2$

questions.q: For a number, greater than one, the difference between itself and its reciprocal is $20\%$ of the sum of itself and its reciprocal. By how much percentage (nearest to an integer) is the square of the number less than its cube?
questions.s:
Dekh bhai, yahan par Algebra + Core Conceptual Tool: 5. Unitary Scaling ka fusion chal raha hai. Pen-Free Observation: Equation frame karo aur Componendo & Dividendo jaisa kuchh dikh jaye toh maza aa jaye. Method 1 (Ninja Technique / Exam Approach): Equation diya hai: $x - \\frac{1}{x} = 0.2 (x + \\frac{1}{x})$. Yani $\\frac{x - 1/x}{x + 1/x} = \\frac{1}{5}$. Cross multiply maar: $5x - \\frac{5}{x} = x + \\frac{1}{x} \\implies 4x = \\frac{6}{x} \\implies x^2 = \\frac{6}{4} = 1.5$. Ab $x = \\sqrt{1.5}$. Pucha hai square ($x^2$), cube ($x^3$) se kitna percentage kam hai? Required % = $\\frac{x^3 - x^2}{x^3} \\times 100 = (1 - \\frac{1}{x}) \\times 100$. $x = \\sqrt{1.5} \\approx 1.224$. $1 / 1.224 \\approx 0.817$. $1 - 0.817 = 0.183 \\implies 18.3\\%$. Nearest integer 18 hoga. Method 2 (Concept Builder): Bina ratio-proportion lagaye sidha algebra khelega toh time lagega, bache hue steps wahi rehte hain. Root approx nikalna aana chahiye (like $\\sqrt{1.44} = 1.2$). Exam Takeaway: Percentage less/more pooche algebra me toh hamesha unka ratio $\\frac{A}{B}$ le lo, absolute values nikalne ki zaroorat nahi hoti.
Ratio TrickFormula
% Less of $A$ wrt $B$$(1 - \\frac{A}{B}) \\times 100$

questions.q: If decreasing 120 by x% gives the same result as increasing 40 by x% then x% of 720 is what percentage more than (x+15)% of 200? (Round off to the nearest integer)
questions.s:
Dekh bhai, ye calculation check karne wala question hai. Ise ham Core Conceptual Tool: 5. Unitary Scaling se break karenge. Pen-Free Observation: 120 ko ghata rahe ho aur 40 ko badha rahe ho to same result aa raha hai. Ratio nikal ke $x$ seedha pata chal sakta hai. Method 1 (Ninja Technique / Exam Approach): $120(1 - \\frac{x}{100}) = 40(1 + \\frac{x}{100})$. 40 se kaat de: $3(100 - x) = 100 + x \\implies 300 - 3x = 100 + x \\implies 4x = 200 \\implies x = 50$. Value of $x$ mil gayi $50$. Ab aage padh: $50\\%$ of 720 pucha hai = 360. Dusri term: $(50+15)\\%$ yani $65\\%$ of 200 = 130. Ab 360, 130 se kitna zyada hai? Gap = 230. Required % = $\\frac{230}{130} \\times 100 = \\frac{2300}{13} \\approx 176.92\\%$. Nearest integer $177\\%$ hit maar! Method 2 (Concept Builder): Steps yahi rahenge, bas percentages ko fractions me likhne se aadat aur tez hoti hai. Equation jaldi solve ho toh rest of the problem halwa hai. Exam Takeaway: Is tarah ke 2-step problems mains me bahut aate hain. Jaldi $x$ nikal ke second statement me ghuso.
Calculation StepExecution
Percentage Gap$\\frac{\\text{Difference}}{\\text{Base Value}} \\times 100$

questions.q: The total cost of 5 pens and 3 notebooks is 130. If the cost of pen is decreased by $25\%$ and that of the notebook is increased by $10\%$ then total cost of 3 pens and 2 notebooks will be 67. what is the total original cost (in) of 6 pens and 4 notebook?
questions.s:
Dekh bhai, yahan par Linear Equations lag rahi hai par hum thoda smartly khelenge. Pen-Free Observation: Equations direct frames kar aur fraction ya decimal se dosti rakh! Method 1 (Ninja Technique / Exam Approach): Eq 1: $5P + 3N = 130$. Eq 2: Pen ka rate $25\\%$ gira yani $0.75P$. Notebook $10\\%$ badhi yani $1.1N$. Nayi Eq: $3(0.75P) + 2(1.1N) = 67 \\implies 2.25P + 2.2N = 67$. Is equation ko 20 se multiply kar de decimal hatane ke liye: $45P + 44N = 1340$. Aur pehli ko 9 se multiply maar: $45P + 27N = 1170$. Dono ko subtract karega toh: $17N = 170 \\implies N = 10$. Put $N = 10$ in Eq 1: $5P + 30 = 130 \\implies 5P = 100 \\implies P = 20$. Pucha kya hai? $6P + 4N = 6(20) + 4(10) = 120 + 40 = 160$. Method 2 (Concept Builder): Variables P aur N leke normal elimination kar, bas decimal me fasne se bacha kar by multiplying with appropriate powers of 10. Exam Takeaway: Decimal equations ko 10 ya 100 se multiply karke whole numbers me le aao, calculation mistakes nahi hongi.
Decimal Removal RuleAction
Avoid float mathMultiply entire equation to remove decimals

questions.q: A man started off a business with a certain capital amount. In the first year, he earned $40\%$ profit and donated $14.28\%$ of the total capital (initial amount + profit). He followed the same procedure with the remaining capital after the second and the third year. If at the end of the three years, he is left with 4320, what was the initial amount with which the man started his business?
questions.s:
Dekh bhai, ye pure Core Conceptual Tool: 2. Successive Change (The Chain Reaction) ka jadoo hai! Pen-Free Observation: Bhai jab bhi same procedure repeat ho raha ho, seedha compounding lagta hai multiplier banake. $14.28\\%$ ko turant $\\frac{1}{7}$ soch lena chahiye. Method 1 (Ninja Technique / Exam Approach): Ek saal ka net multiplier banate hain: Pehle $40\\%$ profit hua, yani value ho gayi $140\\%$ ya $1.4$ times. Fir us total ka $14.28\\%$ (yani $\\frac{1}{7}$ hissa) donate kar diya. Toh bacha kitna? $\\frac{6}{7}$ hissa bacha. Net saal ka multiplier $= 1.4 \\times \\frac{6}{7} = 0.2 \\times 6 = 1.2$. Yani har saal uska paisa $1.2$ guna ho raha hai. 3 saal ke baad: $C \\times (1.2)^3 = 4320$. $C \\times 1.728 = 4320 \\implies C = \\frac{4320}{1.728} = 2500$. Multiplier OP trick hai, ye 20 second me solve karayega! Method 2 (Concept Builder): Har saal ka alag calculate karega toh phansega. $C$, fir $1.4C$, fir usme se minus karega, zindagi nikal jayegi. Compounding ka concept hi isi liye hai. Exam Takeaway: Successive increase/decrease me fraction multiplier banake power me dal diya karo.
Successive FormulaAction
Repeated Process$Final = Initial \\times (m_1 \\times m_2)^n$

questions.q: Suresh decides to donate $46.67\%$ of his monthly salary but later he donates 4900 which is $22.22\%$ less than the amount he planned to donate earlier then find the monthly income of Suresh.
questions.s:
Dekh bhai, yahan par Core Conceptual Tool: 2. Successive Change aur Fraction mastery ka test hai. Pen-Free Observation: Ye ajeeb se percentages dekh ke ghapla nahi karna, inko standard fractions me todo. $46.67\\% = 40\\% + 6.67\\%$ hota hai. Method 1 (Ninja Technique / Exam Approach): Fractions break kar: $46.67\\% = 40\\% + 6.67\\% = \\frac{2}{5} + \\frac{1}{15} = \\frac{6+1}{15} = \\frac{7}{15}$. Ye planned donation thi. Ab $22.22\\% = \\frac{2}{9}$ hota hai. Usne planned se $\\frac{2}{9}$ kam donate kiya, matlab kitna kiya? $\\frac{7}{9}$ of planned amount. Equation bana: $(\\frac{7}{9}) \\times (\\frac{7}{15}) \\times \\text{Income} = 4900$. Numerators dekho: $7 \\times 7 = 49$. Seedha 4900 se kata toh 100 bacha. $\\text{Income} = 100 \\times 9 \\times 15 = 13500$. Sirf 15 seconds ka sawal tha agar fractions aate hon! Method 2 (Concept Builder): Let Income = $x$. Planned = $0.4667x$. Actual = $0.4667x \\times (1 - 0.2222) = 4900$. Is raste jayega toh decimal me doob jayega, bhai. Exam Takeaway: Non-standard percentages ko hamesha base standard percentages me tod kar fraction banaya kar.

questions.q: A stationary supplier ordered 8 boxes of premium pens and some boxes of standard pens. The price of premium pens per box was twice that of standard pens. When the order was delivered, the number of boxes of premium and standard pens had been accidentally interchanged. This increased the total bill by $25\%$. What was the ratio of the original number of premium pens to the original number of boxes of standard pens? (CGL TIER I- $\frac{13}{09}$/2025 - SHIFT 3)
questions.s:
Dekh bhai, ye hai tera Core Conceptual Tool: 4. Cross-Product / Interchange Method ka badiya application. Pen-Free Observation: Price ka ratio Premium(P) aur Standard(S) ka 2:1 hai. Quantity P ki 8 hai aur S ki maan le $x$. Interchange hone pe bill $25\\%$ (yani $1.25$ times) badh gaya. Method 1 (Ninja Technique / Exam Approach): Original Bill = $(8 \\times 2) + (x \\times 1) = 16 + x$. New (Interchanged) Bill = $(x \\times 2) + (8 \\times 1) = 2x + 8$. Question keh raha hai naya bill purane bill se $25\\%$ zyada hai: $(16 + x) \\times 1.25 = (2x + 8)$. $1.25$ ko $\\frac{5}{4}$ likh le easy hoga: $5(16 + x) = 4(2x + 8) \\implies 80 + 5x = 8x + 32 \\implies 3x = 48 \\implies x = 16$. Matlab standard pens originally 16 the. Ratio of original Premium to Standard = $8 : 16 = 1:2$. Boom! Method 2 (Concept Builder): Isko options put karke bhi uda sakte the. Agar $1:2$ le, matlab standard boxes 16 hain. Purana bill = $8(2) + 16(1) = 32$. Naya bill = $16(2) + 8(1) = 40$. Increment $= 40-32 = 8$. % Increment $= (8/32) \\times 100 = 25\\%$. Options check is even faster! Exam Takeaway: Interchange wale questions me options plug karna sabse khatarnak shortcut hota hai.
